color_palette.name: Brutalk Black
color_palette.usage: Dominant background across all pages and card surfaces — the raw, unlit canvas that makes every other element hit harder. Used in nav bars, hero backgrounds, footer, and the base of all dark-mode card tiles in the class and schedule grids.

color_palette.name: Chalk Strike
color_palette.usage: Primary text color on dark surfaces, hero headlines, instructor names, pricing plan labels, and schedule timetable entries. The near-white is deliberately not pure white — it reads like chalk on a blackboard, matching the raw, hand-posted aesthetic.

color_palette.name: Alarm Red
color_palette.usage: The single aggressive accent — used for primary CTAs ('Book a Seat', 'Start Now'), active nav states, card hover borders, stat callout numbers on the home and pricing pages, and the brand logotype mark. Saturated to the point of confrontation.

color_palette.name: Hyperlink Blue
color_palette.usage: Default-looking browser-blue applied deliberately as a brutalist visual cue — used for secondary links, FAQ answer toggles, inline text links in instructor bios and class descriptions, and comparison table highlights. Signals raw, unstyled intentionality.

color_palette.name: Concrete Slab
color_palette.usage: Secondary card surface and section divider background — one step lighter than Brutalk Black, used to separate card grid tiles from the page background without softening the rawness. Appears in class cards, schedule row alternates, and pricing plan containers.

color_palette.name: Caution Stripe
color_palette.usage: High-visibility accent for warning-register moments: featured class badges, 'SOLD OUT' and 'LAST SEATS' labels on schedule cards, the most-popular pricing plan border highlight, and stat labels on the home and schedule pages. Harsh contrast against black — zero subtlety intended.

typography.heading_treatment: Arial Black (system web-safe heavy grotesque) at aggressive display scale — H1 at 96–120px on desktop, fully uppercase, tracking at -0.02em to compress the mass, zero border-radius energy. H2 at 56–72px uppercase. H3 at 32–40px uppercase. Weight never drops below 900. No decorative flourish — the type IS the design object. Asymmetric alignment encouraged: left-flush on hero, hard-left on cards, occasional full-bleed oversized single-word treatments that bleed off the card edge.
typography.body_treatment: Courier New monospace at 15–16px, line-height 1.6, normal weight. Body copy reads like a typed document or a printed timetable — functional, unbeautified, and deliberately low-design. Used in class descriptions, instructor bios, FAQ answers, schedule details, and pricing plan feature lists. Reinforces the 'no-frills, just information' voice of BRUTALK.
typography.accent_treatment: VT323 (Google Fonts CRT terminal face) at 12–14px only — reserved for eyebrow labels above section headings, card metadata (language level tags, session duration, seat count), stat unit labels, and badge text. Never used at display scale. Evokes a raw data-terminal readout, reinforcing the anti-polish brutalist register without drifting into cyberpunk.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
## BRUTALK Home Page — Visual Design Plan

### Page Role & Tone
This is the brand's first and loudest statement. Every section must feel like it was posted on a concrete wall — confrontational, functional, and impossible to ignore. No softening. No modern-SaaS polish. The page is built from raw structural blocks, oversized type, harsh contrast, and deliberate asymmetry.

---

### Section Sequence & Rhythm

1. **Hero** — Full-bleed black slab. Oversized uppercase type dominates. Maximum density, zero whitespace generosity. The brand arrives like a punch.
2. **Stats** — A horizontal marquee strip of four massive numerals scrolling continuously. Sparse, kinetic, and loud. Breaks the vertical stacking rhythm entirely.
3. **Feature Grid** — A dense, asymmetric 3-column card grid on dark concrete surface. Cards have visible hard borders, no radius. Staggered reveal on scroll.
4. **Testimonials** — Three raw quote blocks arranged in an off-grid, deliberately uneven horizontal layout. Human warmth expressed through monospace type and hard structural edges, not softness.
5. **CTA Close** — Full-bleed Alarm Red panel with the language-code typographic tile pattern as background texture. The loudest color moment on the page. Single dominant headline. Kicks the door open.

Rhythm alternates: dense/kinetic → sparse/kinetic → dense/static → medium/human → explosive/color. No two consecutive sections share the same density or motion register.

---

### Signature Moment
**The Stats Marquee Strip (Section 2)** is the page's signature visual and motion moment. The four stat figures — 12,400+, 94%, 18 Languages, 200+ Instructors — are rendered in Arial Black at 96–120px in Alarm Red (#E8000D) and scroll continuously left in a seamless loop against a Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background, separated by bold slash dividers in Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2). This is a full-bleed horizontal band with no vertical padding — it reads like a ticker tape ripped from a stock exchange or a stadium scoreboard. The motion is relentless, ambient, and never pauses. This is the single most memorable visual gesture on the page: it turns data into kinetic spectacle, it's unmistakably brutalist in its anti-decorative function, and it uses Alarm Red at full amplitude as a typographic color rather than a UI accent. No other page in the site has this treatment.

---

### Color & Surface Logic
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background. Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) for headline and subheadline. Alarm Red (#E8000D) for the eyebrow label and the primary CTA button. Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) for the secondary CTA link (raw browser-blue, unstyled appearance).
- **Section 2 (Stats Marquee):** Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background. Alarm Red (#E8000D) for the stat numbers. Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) for dividers and descriptor labels. No other colors.
- **Section 3 (Feature Grid):** Concrete Slab (#1E1E1E) section background. Card surfaces in Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) with 2px Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) borders. Eyebrow in Caution Stripe (#FFD600). Headline in Chalk Strike. Card titles in Chalk Strike at H3 scale. Body in Courier New monospace, Chalk Strike at reduced opacity (~70%). CTA link in Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE).
- **Section 4 (Testimonials):** Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background. Quote text in Chalk Strike. Attribution in Caution Stripe (#FFD600) for name, VT323 accent font for language/level metadata. Hard left-border rules in Alarm Red (#E8000D) on each quote block — 4px solid.
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Alarm Red (#E8000D) full-bleed background — the only full-bleed red panel on the page. Headline in Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) — inverted from all other sections. Eyebrow in Caution Stripe (#FFD600). Primary CTA button in Brutalk Black with Chalk Strike text. Secondary CTA link in Brutalk Black underlined. Language-code tile pattern rendered at 10% opacity in Brutalk Black over the red background.

---

### Typography Hierarchy
- **H1 (Hero headline):** Arial Black, 96–120px desktop / 52px mobile, uppercase, tracking -0.02em, left-aligned, Chalk Strike. The word "GAMES" in the headline bleeds slightly beyond the grid container on the right edge — a deliberate off-grid stunt.
- **H2 (Section headlines):** Arial Black, 56–72px desktop / 36px mobile, uppercase, left-aligned (except Section 5 CTA which is centered).
- **H3 (Card titles, quote attributions):** Arial Black, 32–40px desktop / 24px mobile, uppercase, left-aligned.
- **Eyebrows:** VT323, 13px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em — used as terminal-readout labels above section headlines.
- **Body / descriptions:** Courier New monospace, 15–16px, line-height 1.6, Chalk Strike at 70% opacity on dark surfaces.
- **Stat numbers (marquee):** Arial Black, 96px, Alarm Red — these are display objects, not data labels.
- **Stat descriptors (marquee):** Courier New, 14px, Chalk Strike — small, functional, below the number.
- **Badge / metadata:** VT323, 12–13px, Caution Stripe on dark, or Brutalk Black on light.

---

### Motion Design

**On-Load Arc:**
The page loads with Brutalk Black already filling the screen. The BRUTALK wordmark logo slams in from the top-left with a fast, zero-easing translate — no fade, just a hard positional snap — as if it was always there and the page just revealed it. A beat after the logo settles, the H1 headline appears line by line: "STOP PLAYING" drops in first (translates up from 20px below, no opacity fade — just movement), then "GAMES. START" a half-beat later, then "SPEAKING." last. The subheadline types in character by character in Courier New — a blinking cursor appears, types the full text at a brisk pace, then the cursor disappears. The two CTAs slide in from the left together, a beat after the subheadline finishes. Total on-load arc: approximately 2.5 seconds.

**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
- Section 3 (Feature Grid): Cards stagger in as the section enters the viewport. Each card translates up 24px and snaps into place in sequence — left column first, then middle, then right — with a short delay between each card. No opacity fade — just hard positional movement, matching the brutalist no-softness rule.
- Section 4 (Testimonials): The three quote blocks slide in from the left simultaneously as the section enters view, but at slightly different distances (first block 16px, second 32px, third 48px) so they arrive at slightly different times — creating an organic, uneven stagger that reads as human rather than mechanical.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): The Alarm Red background panel flashes on instantly (no fade) as the section enters view — a hard color cut. Then the headline slams down from above (translate -30px to 0) a beat later. The CTAs appear last.

**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
- Hero CTAs: Primary (Alarm Red) button shifts to Chalk Strike background with Alarm Red text on hover — a hard color inversion, no transition softening beyond 80ms. Secondary link underline grows from 1px to 3px on hover.
- Feature Grid cards: On hover, the 2px Chalk Strike border switches to 2px Alarm Red border, and the card translates up 4px. No shadow (brutalist — no depth illusion). Focus state matches hover state with a visible outline.
- Testimonial quote blocks: On hover, the left Alarm Red border thickens from 4px to 8px instantly. No other change.
- CTA close buttons: On hover, the Brutalk Black button inverts to Chalk Strike background with Brutalk Black text.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- **Stats Marquee (Section 2):** The strip scrolls left continuously at a steady, hypnotic pace — fast enough to feel alive, slow enough to read each figure. Loops seamlessly. This is the page's primary ambient motion and the signature motion moment. It never pauses, never eases — constant velocity, like a machine running.
- **Hero cursor:** The blinking text cursor that appears during the subheadline type-in effect disappears after typing completes. No further ambient cursor blink — the type-in is a one-time on-load gesture, not a loop.
- **CTA close section:** The language-code tile pattern (ES, FR, DE, ZH, JP, AR) in the background drifts very slowly upward in a seamless parallax loop — barely perceptible, like heat rising off asphalt. It reinforces the texture without competing with the headline.

**Signature Motion Moment:**
The Stats Marquee strip (Section 2) is both the signature visual and the signature motion moment. The continuous left-scroll of 96px Alarm Red numerals against pure black — with no pause, no easing, no hover-stop — is the most kinetically aggressive gesture on the page. It is the one place where motion IS the design, not a decoration on top of it. This is calibrated correctly for brutalism: one bold structural motion gesture, not six subtle micro-interactions.

---

### Density & Whitespace Logic
- **Hero:** Zero generous whitespace. Top padding is tight — the headline starts high on the viewport. The wordmark and eyebrow are stacked immediately. The visual mass of the type IS the hero image.
- **Stats Marquee:** No vertical padding — the strip is exactly as tall as the type plus minimal clearance. It is a band, not a section.
- **Feature Grid:** 24px internal card padding. 16px grid gaps. The section has 80px top/bottom padding on desktop. Dense but structured.
- **Testimonials:** 64px top/bottom padding. Quote blocks have generous internal space for the text but the section itself is not airy — three blocks side by side keep the density.
- **CTA Close:** 120px top/bottom padding. Sparse — one eyebrow, one headline, one subheadline, two CTAs. The red does the heavy lifting; the type doesn't need to crowd it.

---

### Responsive Behavior
- **Mobile (< 768px):** Hero headline drops to 52px, single column. Stats marquee remains full-bleed but the numeral size drops to 64px. Feature grid collapses to single column, cards stack vertically. Testimonials stack vertically, each quote block full-width. CTA close headline drops to 40px, CTAs stack vertically.
- **Tablet (768–1024px):** Feature grid becomes 2-column. Testimonials remain 3-column but with tighter gaps. Hero headline at 72px.
- **Desktop (1024px+):** All layouts as specified — 3-column feature grid, 3-column testimonials, full marquee speed.

---

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses every color in the palette with intentionality: Brutalk Black and Concrete Slab as surfaces, Chalk Strike as primary text, Alarm Red as the dominant accent (marquee numerals, eyebrow on hero, CTA, left-border rules, CTA close background), Hyperlink Blue as secondary link treatment, Caution Stripe for testimonial attributions and the CTA close eyebrow. The typography hierarchy is strictly observed. The page is the loudest in the site — it must establish the register that all other pages operate within.

section_design_plans.nl_prompt:
**Section 1 — Hero**

Full-bleed Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background, zero border-radius anywhere. No photography, no illustration — the type IS the hero image.

**Layout:** Single-column, hard left-aligned, full viewport height (100vh minimum). No centered content. The BRUTALK wordmark logo asset sits at the very top-left of the section, inside the content area (not the nav) — it is large, rendered in Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) with the diagonal slash detail cutting through the letterforms in Alarm Red (#E8000D). It reads as a brand stamp, not a navigation element.

**Eyebrow:** VT323 font, 13px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em, Alarm Red (#E8000D), positioned immediately below the wordmark. Text: 'Language Learning. Unfiltered.' — reads like a terminal classification tag.

**Headline:** Arial Black, 96–120px on desktop (52px mobile), fully uppercase, tracking -0.02em, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-aligned. Text: 'STOP PLAYING GAMES. START SPEAKING.' — rendered across three lines for maximum vertical mass. The word 'GAMES.' on line two is intentionally set so its right edge bleeds 20–30px beyond the standard content grid boundary — a deliberate off-grid stunt that signals rule-breaking and creates visual tension. This is a typographic signature move for this section.

**Subheadline:** Courier New monospace, 16px, line-height 1.6, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) at 80% opacity. Text: 'BRUTALK is the structured language platform for people who want fluency, not points. Real instructors, real classes, real results.' Left-aligned, maximum width 600px — does not span the full viewport. Appears via a type-in animation on load: characters appear one by one at a brisk pace with a blinking cursor, then the cursor disappears when typing completes.

**CTAs:** Two controls, left-aligned, stacked horizontally with 24px gap. Primary: 'See All Classes' — rendered as a raw HTML-default-looking button in Alarm Red (#E8000D) background, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) text, Arial Black 14px uppercase, no border-radius, 2px solid Alarm Red border, 12px 24px padding. On hover: hard color inversion to Chalk Strike background / Alarm Red text in 80ms — no easing softness. Secondary: 'View Pricing' — rendered as a bare Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) text link, Courier New 15px, underline always visible (1px), no button chrome. On hover: underline thickens to 3px. Both controls receive visible focus outlines for keyboard navigation.

**Spacing:** 48px top padding from viewport top (below nav). 80px bottom padding. The section feels top-heavy and dense — the type mass starts high and the CTAs land low.

**Motion (on-load arc):** The wordmark logo snaps in from the top-left with a fast hard translate (no fade, no easing — just positional snap) as the very first element. A beat later, the headline lines drop in sequentially: line 1 translates up 20px into position, then line 2 a half-beat after, then line 3. No opacity change — pure positional movement, matching brutalist no-softness rule. After the headline settles, the subheadline begins its type-in character-by-character sequence with a blinking cursor. The two CTAs slide in from the left together a beat after the subheadline finishes typing. Total arc: approximately 2.5 seconds.

**This section is deliberately still after the on-load arc** — no ambient loops, no parallax. The type holds the weight alone.

**Section 2 — Stats (The Signature Moment)**

This section IS the page's signature visual and motion moment. It is NOT a conventional stats grid. It is a full-bleed horizontal marquee band — a continuously scrolling ticker strip of four massive stat figures rendered in Alarm Red (#E8000D) against Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A).

**Layout:** Full viewport width, no content container constraints. The band's height is determined purely by the type size plus minimal top/bottom clearance — approximately 140–160px total height. No section padding beyond 16px top and bottom. It reads as a structural band on the page, not a content section with breathing room.

**Eyebrow and headline:** The eyebrow ('The Numbers Don't Lie') and headline ('Results That Speak for Themselves') are placed ABOVE the marquee band, left-aligned within the standard content container, on a Brutalk Black background. Eyebrow: VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600), uppercase. Headline: Arial Black, 56px desktop / 32px mobile, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2). These two lines are tight — 8px gap between eyebrow and headline, 24px gap between headline and the marquee band below.

**Marquee content:** The four stat items scroll left in a seamless continuous loop. Each item is a paired unit: the stat number (Arial Black, 96px desktop / 64px mobile, Alarm Red #E8000D, uppercase) stacked above its descriptor label (Courier New, 14px, Chalk Strike #F2F2F2, normal weight). Between each item: a bold vertical slash divider ' / ' in Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) at 96px height — rendered as a typographic character, not a drawn line. The sequence: '12,400+' / '94%' / '18 LANGUAGES' / '200+ INSTRUCTORS' / [loop repeats]. The content is duplicated in the DOM to create a seamless loop.

**Motion:** The marquee scrolls left at a constant, steady velocity — fast enough to feel kinetic and alive (approximately the pace of a stock ticker), slow enough that each figure is fully readable as it passes through the center of the viewport. The scroll never pauses, never eases, never stops — it is machine-constant. No hover-to-pause behavior. This relentlessness is intentional and brutalist.

**Color emphasis:** This is the only section where Alarm Red (#E8000D) occupies the majority of the visual field as typographic color rather than UI chrome. The red numerals at 96px against pure black create the harshest contrast on the page — intentional confrontation.

**Responsive:** On mobile, numerals drop to 64px. The scroll speed adjusts proportionally so the reading pace feels the same. The section height reduces to approximately 100px.

**This section has no CTA, no card structure, no grid.** It is a pure kinetic data statement. It breaks the vertical rhythm of the page entirely — a horizontal machine inserted between two denser sections.

**Section 3 — Feature Grid**

Concrete Slab (#1E1E1E) section background — one step lighter than the hero's Brutalk Black, creating a visible surface change without any softness. This section is the most structurally dense content block on the page.

**Layout:** Standard content container (max-width 1280px, centered). 80px top/bottom padding on desktop. 3-column grid on desktop (each column approximately equal width, 16px gaps), 2-column on tablet, 1-column on mobile.

**Eyebrow:** VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600), uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em. Text: 'Why BRUTALK Works'. Left-aligned above the headline.

**Headline:** Arial Black, 64px desktop / 36px mobile, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-aligned. Text: 'WE CUT EVERYTHING THAT DOESN'T MAKE YOU FLUENT'. Rendered across two lines, no centering.

**Subheadline:** Courier New, 16px, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) at 70% opacity, left-aligned, max-width 640px. Text: 'No streaks. No badges. No filler. Just the mechanics of language acquisition done right.' 24px gap below before the card grid begins.

**Cards (6 total):** Each card is a hard rectangular tile — Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background, 2px solid Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) border, zero border-radius, 24px internal padding. No shadow, no depth effect.

- **Card title:** Arial Black, 24px, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-aligned.
- **Card body:** Courier New, 15px, line-height 1.6, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) at 65% opacity, left-aligned.
- No icons, no illustrations — type only. The structure of the text IS the visual.
- Cards are equal height within each row (CSS grid stretch behavior).

**Card hover state:** On hover, the 2px Chalk Strike border switches instantly to 2px Alarm Red (#E8000D) border, and the card translates up 4px. No shadow added (brutalist — no depth illusion). Transition on border-color: 80ms, no easing. Focus state mirrors hover state with an additional visible outline.

**CTA:** Below the 6-card grid, left-aligned, 32px gap from the last card row. 'Explore the Classes' rendered as a Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) text link, Courier New 15px, underline always visible. On hover: underline thickens to 3px.

**Scroll-triggered motion:** As the section enters the viewport via IntersectionObserver, the six cards stagger in sequentially — each card translates up 24px into its final position. Left column cards first (top to bottom), then middle column, then right column. Each card snaps into position with a short delay between cards — no opacity fade, pure positional movement. The stagger makes the grid feel like it's being assembled in real time.

**Asymmetric detail:** The sixth card (Community Practice Rooms) in the bottom-right cell of the grid is given a Caution Stripe (#FFD600) 2px border instead of Chalk Strike — a deliberate asymmetric accent that breaks the visual uniformity and rewards close attention. Its hover state still switches to Alarm Red.

**Section 4 — Testimonials**

Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background — returns to the hero's base surface. This section provides human warmth without abandoning the raw aesthetic. No photography, no avatars, no star ratings — just words and structural markers.

**Layout:** Standard content container. 64px top/bottom padding. Three quote blocks arranged in a horizontal row on desktop — NOT equal-width columns. The blocks are deliberately uneven: left block takes approximately 38% width, center block approximately 30%, right block approximately 32%. This asymmetry is intentional — it resists the three-equal-column template and creates visual tension.

**Eyebrow:** VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600), uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em. Text: 'Heard From the Trenches'. Left-aligned above the headline.

**Headline:** Arial Black, 56px desktop / 32px mobile, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-aligned. Text: 'PEOPLE WHO STOPPED DABBLING AND STARTED SPEAKING'. Rendered across two lines.

**Quote blocks (3 total):** Each block has:
- A 4px solid Alarm Red (#E8000D) left border — the primary structural marker. This is the visual anchor of each quote block. On hover, this border thickens instantly from 4px to 8px — no transition, a hard snap, like a stamp being pressed harder.
- 16px left padding from the red border to the text.
- **Quote text:** Courier New, 15px, line-height 1.7, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) at 85% opacity. The quotation marks are large — rendered in Arial Black at 48px in Alarm Red (#E8000D), positioned as a typographic drop-cap above the quote text (not inline). This gives each block a visual anchor point.
- **Attribution line:** Arial Black, 18px, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2). Text: e.g. 'MARTA V. — SPANISH → GERMAN, B2'.
- **Metadata badge:** VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600). Text: e.g. 'GERMAN / B2' — appears below the attribution as a terminal-readout tag.
- No card border, no background fill on the blocks — they float on the black surface, anchored only by the red left border.

**Scroll-triggered motion:** As the section enters the viewport, all three quote blocks slide in from the left simultaneously, but at slightly different travel distances: left block 16px, center block 32px, right block 48px. Because they all start moving at the same time but travel different distances, they arrive at their final positions at slightly different moments — creating an organic, uneven stagger that feels human rather than mechanical. No opacity fade — pure positional movement.

**Mobile:** Blocks stack vertically, full width, 32px gap between them. The asymmetric widths collapse to equal full-width.

**This section is deliberately still after its scroll entrance** — no ambient motion. The red borders hold the weight.

**Section 5 — CTA Close**

This is the loudest color moment on the entire page and the final aggressive close. The section background is a full-bleed Alarm Red (#E8000D) panel — the only full-bleed red surface on the page. It signals finality and urgency through color alone before the visitor reads a word.

**Background texture:** The language-code tile pattern asset (repeating block letterforms: ES, FR, DE, ZH, JP, AR in a dense offset brick-like tiling) is placed as a full-bleed background layer behind all content, rendered in Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) at 10% opacity over the red. The pattern is not centered or cropped — it tiles edge-to-edge, bleeding off all four sides. This creates a subtle kinetic texture that signals linguistic breadth without photography. The pattern drifts very slowly upward in a seamless ambient parallax loop — barely perceptible, like heat rising off asphalt. This is the only ambient loop in this section.

**Layout:** Content container (max-width 1280px), centered horizontally. 120px top/bottom padding. All text is centered — this is the one section on the page where centering is used, because the brutalist close demands a monolithic, confrontational symmetry. The visitor has nowhere to look but straight at the message.

**Eyebrow:** VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600), uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em. Text: 'No More Excuses'. Centered.

**Headline:** Arial Black, 72px desktop / 40px mobile, uppercase, Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) — inverted from every other headline on the page (dark text on red background). Text: 'PICK A LANGUAGE. BOOK A CLASS. SHOW UP.' Three imperative sentences, each on its own line, each landing like a separate command. Tracking -0.02em.

**Subheadline:** Courier New, 16px, Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) at 80% opacity, centered, max-width 560px, line-height 1.6. Text: 'Your next cohort starts this week. Seats are capped. First session is on us.' The monospace type on the red surface reads like a notice pinned to a board.

**CTAs:** Two controls, centered, stacked horizontally with 24px gap. Primary: 'Claim Your Free First Class' — Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) text, Arial Black 14px uppercase, no border-radius, 2px solid Brutalk Black border, 14px 28px padding. On hover: hard inversion to Chalk Strike background / Brutalk Black text in 80ms. Secondary: 'See the Schedule' — Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) text link, Courier New 15px, underline always visible (1px). On hover: underline thickens to 3px.

**Scroll-triggered motion:** As the section enters the viewport, the Alarm Red background panel flashes on instantly — a hard color cut with no fade. A beat later, the headline slams down from 30px above its final position into place (translate -30px to 0, no opacity fade). The subheadline and CTAs appear a beat after the headline lands.

**No other ambient motion in this section beyond the slow background pattern drift.** The red does the heavy lifting — additional motion would compete with it.

**Mobile:** Headline drops to 40px, CTAs stack vertically with 16px gap. Pattern tile continues to drift upward at the same pace.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
BRUTALK CLASSES PAGE — FULL PAGE DESIGN DIRECTION

SURFACE & COLOR LOGIC ACROSS THE PAGE:
The page sits on Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) as its dominant canvas. Sections alternate between Brutalk Black and Concrete Slab (#1E1E1E) surfaces — but not in a polite, even rhythm. The header section is pure black with a full-bleed typographic illustration. The card grid sits on Concrete Slab. The comparison section punches back to black with a Alarm Red (#E8000D) structural rule running the full width as a divider. The FAQ section returns to Concrete Slab. The closing CTA section is a full-bleed Alarm Red panel — the only section where red dominates the background, making it feel like a fire alarm at the bottom of the page. Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) appears as inline text links and comparison table positive indicators. Caution Stripe (#FFD600) appears on card badges and metadata labels. Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) is the primary text color throughout.

TYPOGRAPHIC HIERARCHY:
H1 (page header): Arial Black, 96–120px, fully uppercase, tracking -0.02em, left-flush, Chalk Strike on black. The headline "18 Languages. 6 Levels. Zero Filler." is treated as three stacked slabs — each phrase on its own line, the word "ZERO" rendered at 120px and bleeds slightly past the right grid boundary, creating the signature off-grid tension. H2 (section headlines): Arial Black, 56–72px, uppercase, left-flush. H3 (card titles): Arial Black, 28–32px, uppercase. Body: Courier New, 15–16px, line-height 1.6. Eyebrow labels: VT323, 13–14px, uppercase, Caution Stripe or Alarm Red depending on surface. The comparison table uses Courier New for all data rows. The FAQ uses Courier New for both questions (bold, 18px) and answers (regular, 15px).

SECTION RHYTHM & DENSITY:
Section 1 (page header): Sparse — big type, one illustration asset, lots of black air. Section 2 (card grid): Dense — 8 cards in a 4-column grid on desktop, 2-column on tablet, 1-column on mobile, staggered scroll reveal. Section 3 (comparison): Medium density — a hard-ruled table structure, no decorative softening. Section 4 (FAQ): Medium density — accordion-style list, icon set anchored to the left. Section 5 (CTA): Sparse — full-bleed red, two lines of type, two buttons. The rhythm is: SPARSE → DENSE → MEDIUM → MEDIUM → SPARSE. This creates a breathing pattern that prevents fatigue while keeping the brutalist rawness throughout.

SIGNATURE MOMENT — "THE BLEED WORD":
In Section 1 (page header), the word "ZERO" in the headline "18 Languages. 6 Levels. Zero Filler." is rendered at 120px in Arial Black, Alarm Red, fully uppercase, and intentionally overflows the right edge of the content grid — it bleeds past the container boundary by approximately 60–80px, cropped by the viewport edge. This is the page's defining typographic stunt. It signals immediately that BRUTALK does not stay inside comfortable boxes. The rest of the headline sits in Chalk Strike at the same scale, making "ZERO" a color-and-overflow double punch. This move is 100% brutalist — structural, unapologetic, and impossible to miss.

SIGNATURE MOTION MOMENT — "THE BLEED WORD SLAM":
On page load, the three headline lines drop in sequentially from above — each slab slides down and locks into place with a hard stop (no bounce, no ease-out softness — a stark, mechanical snap). "18 Languages." lands first. "6 Levels." lands a beat later. "ZERO FILLER." lands last and simultaneously the word "ZERO" in Alarm Red appears to slam rightward by about 8px past its resting position before snapping back — a single, violent overshoot that settles in one frame. This is the signature motion moment. It is loud, structural, and belongs entirely to the brutalist register.

ON-LOAD ARC:
1. Page arrives: Brutalk Black background fills instantly — no fade in.
2. Eyebrow label "THE FULL CATALOG" in VT323 appears first, blinking once like a terminal cursor activating.
3. Headline slabs drop in sequentially (described above as signature motion moment).
4. Subheadline fades in in Courier New, a beat after the headline settles.
5. The typographic globe illustration fades in slowly from 0 opacity over about 600ms — it does not animate with motion, just materializes.
6. Nav and page chrome are already visible — no nav animation.

SCROLL-TRIGGERED REVEALS:
- Section 2 (card grid): Cards stagger in from bottom — each card translates up 24px and fades from 0 to 1 opacity, staggered by roughly half a beat per card, left-to-right, top-to-bottom. This gives the catalog a kinetic "posting to a wall" energy.
- Section 3 (comparison): The full-width Alarm Red horizontal rule draws from left to right before the table rows appear. Each row fades in sequentially top-to-bottom, a beat apart.
- Section 4 (FAQ): The icon set slides in from the left. FAQ items cascade in from top-to-bottom with a short fade.
- Section 5 (CTA): The entire red panel snaps into view — no fade, just an instant reveal that feels like a klaxon firing.

HOVER AFFORDANCES:
- Class cards: On hover, a 3px Alarm Red border appears on all four sides of the card (replacing the default 1px Concrete Slab border), and the card title shifts to Alarm Red. No lift, no shadow — brutalism doesn't float.
- CTA buttons: On hover, the button background and text invert — if the button is Alarm Red with Chalk Strike text, it becomes Chalk Strike with Alarm Red text. Hard swap, no transition duration longer than 80ms.
- FAQ accordion items: On hover, the question text shifts to Hyperlink Blue. On click/expand, the answer reveals with a fast expand (no smooth ease — a quick mechanical snap open).
- Comparison table rows: On hover, the entire row background shifts to a 15% opacity Alarm Red tint, making the row feel highlighted like a scanner passing over it.
- Navigation links (inherited): Hyperlink Blue underline appears on hover.

AMBIENT LOOPED MOTION:
One ambient motion only — brutalist restraint. In the closing CTA section (Section 5), the primary "View the Schedule" button has a slow, steady pulse on its border: a 2px Chalk Strike border that fades in and out on a 2-second loop, like a heartbeat monitor. This is the only looped ambient motion on the page. Everything else is still when not being interacted with.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR:
- Desktop (1280px+): 4-column card grid, full-bleed type overflow on "ZERO", comparison table at full width, FAQ with icon set in left column.
- Tablet (768–1279px): 2-column card grid, "ZERO" overflow reduced to ~30px bleed, comparison table scrollable horizontally if needed, FAQ icon set stacks above questions.
- Mobile (< 768px): 1-column card grid, "ZERO" overflow removed — headline stacks cleanly, comparison table becomes a stacked card format (one row per card), FAQ is full-width accordion. The closing CTA red panel remains full-bleed at all breakpoints.

FIT WITHIN SHARED DESIGN SYSTEM:
This page uses only the six defined palette colors, both heading and body fonts from the shared system, and VT323 for accent labels. No new colors, no new fonts. The brutalist rawness is achieved through scale, overflow, hard swaps, and structural color — not through new design elements. The page feels like a sibling to Home but with its own catalog-specific energy: where Home hits once hard, the Classes page hits repeatedly through the staggered card grid, building cumulative pressure toward enrollment.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
BRUTALK SCHEDULE PAGE — Full Design Direction

OVERVIEW & RHYTHM
This page is a working tool, not a marketing surface. It should feel like a timetable torn off a wall and digitized — raw, authoritative, information-dense, and confrontational in its clarity. The five sections alternate between maximum density (the session grid) and stark, structural moments (stats, story block, CTA close), creating a rhythm of LOUD → FUNCTIONAL → LOUD → STILL → LOUD. No section should feel like a polished SaaS template — every layout move leans into the brutalist card-grid vocabulary.

Section sequence:
1. Page Header — masthead-style, functional, no decoration
2. Session Grid — the core timetable, dense card grid, the page's primary body
3. Stats Strip — horizontal data blast, oversized numerals, tight and fast
4. Story Block — asymmetric two-column split, type-heavy, deliberately still
5. CTA Close — full-bleed Alarm Red panel, single confrontational headline

SIGNATURE MOMENT
The page's signature visual moment lives in Section 2 (Session Grid): a full-bleed, oversized single word — "SESSIONS" — rendered in Arial Black at approximately 200–240px, uppercase, in Caution Stripe (#FFD600) on Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A), positioned behind the grid as a background typographic layer. The word bleeds off the right edge of the viewport, partially obscured by the card grid sitting on top of it. This is a brutalist type-as-texture move — the oversized word becomes structural wallpaper, raw and confrontational, making the grid feel like it's been bolted onto a live timetable board. It is unmistakably BRUTALK and belongs to the Raw Brutalist aesthetic at full amplitude.

SIGNATURE MOTION MOMENT
Tied to the signature visual: as Section 2 scrolls into view, the oversized "SESSIONS" background word slides in slowly from the right — a heavy, deliberate horizontal drift that settles into its bleed position a beat after the section heading snaps in. It moves once and stops. No loop. This single structural gesture gives the grid its kinetic authority without over-animating the page.

ON-LOAD ARC
- The page header (Section 1) is the first thing that loads. The eyebrow label in VT323 blinks once like a terminal cursor activating, then holds. A beat later, the headline slams in from the left — a fast, heavy horizontal slide that feels like a physical impact. The subheadline fades in a half-beat after the headline settles.
- No page-load gradient sweep, no hero illustration drift. The brutalist register demands restraint on load — one strong move, not a cascade.

SCROLL-TRIGGERED REVEALS
- Section 2 (Grid): the section headline snaps in first (fast slide-up), then the oversized "SESSIONS" background word drifts in from the right (slow, deliberate). Cards stagger in from left-to-right in rows of 3, each card sliding up and fading in with a short delay between them — the stagger makes the volume of sessions feel abundant and alive.
- Section 3 (Stats): the four stat numbers count up from zero as they enter the viewport — a raw, mechanical count-up that reinforces the "live platform" feeling. Stat labels appear simultaneously with no additional animation.
- Section 4 (Story Block): the chart asset slides in from the right as the text column fades up from below — two independent motions that arrive at roughly the same time, creating visual tension without choreography.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): the Alarm Red panel cuts in with a hard vertical wipe from left to right — no fade, no ease. The headline snaps in immediately after the wipe completes.

HOVER & FOCUS AFFORDANCES
- Session cards: on hover, a 3px Alarm Red (#E8000D) border appears on all four sides simultaneously (no transition easing — it snaps on), and the card surface lifts 4px with a hard box-shadow in Alarm Red at low opacity. Cards with 0 seats remaining (SOLD OUT / WAITLIST) do not lift — instead, the border turns Caution Stripe (#FFD600) on hover to signal the different state.
- "Book a Seat" buttons on cards: on hover, background flips from Alarm Red to Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) with text flipping to Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) — a hard, instantaneous color swap with no gradient transition.
- CTA section buttons: same hard color-swap behavior.
- Nav items and secondary links: Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) underline appears on hover, no other change — deliberately browser-default in feel.

AMBIENT LOOPED MOTION
- The "LAST SEAT" and "SOLD OUT" badge labels on session cards pulse slowly — a gentle opacity oscillation between 100% and 70% every two seconds — suggesting live, real-time seat status without manufactured urgency.
- No marquee strips, no gradient sweeps. Brutalist register: one ambient loop, structural and purposeful.

COLOR & SURFACE LOGIC
- Sections 1, 2: Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background — the raw canvas
- Section 3 (Stats): Concrete Slab (#1E1E1E) background — one step lighter, creates visual separation without softening
- Section 4 (Story Block): Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background — returns to raw canvas for the quiet moment
- Section 5 (CTA Close): Alarm Red (#E8000D) full-bleed panel — the single saturated break that closes the page with confrontational energy
- Session cards: Concrete Slab (#1E1E1E) surface, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) text, Caution Stripe (#FFD600) for seat-count badges and warning states
- Alarm Red used on: primary CTAs, active card hover borders, the CTA panel background
- Hyperlink Blue used on: instructor name links, secondary navigation links, "See All Instructors" link
- Caution Stripe used on: "LAST SEAT" / "SOLD OUT" badges, the oversized background word in Section 2

TYPOGRAPHIC HIERARCHY
- H1 (page header headline): Arial Black, 96px desktop / 56px mobile, uppercase, left-flush, Chalk Strike on Brutalk Black, tracking -0.02em
- H2 (section headlines): Arial Black, 56–72px desktop / 36px mobile, uppercase, left-flush, Chalk Strike
- Card titles: Arial Black, 22–24px, uppercase, Chalk Strike
- Eyebrow labels: VT323, 13px, uppercase, Caution Stripe or Alarm Red depending on section
- Body / card descriptions: Courier New, 15px, line-height 1.6, Chalk Strike at 80% opacity
- Stat numerals: Arial Black, 72–80px, uppercase, Chalk Strike with Alarm Red for the numeral itself
- Stat labels: VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe
- CTA close headline: Arial Black, 80–96px desktop, uppercase, Chalk Strike on Alarm Red

DENSITY & WHITESPACE LOGIC
- Section 1: generous top padding (80px), tight bottom padding (40px) — functional masthead, not a hero
- Section 2: dense — minimal padding between cards (16px gutter), the grid fills the full container width
- Section 3: tight horizontal strip — 24px top/bottom padding, stats in a single row with heavy gutters between them
- Section 4: 80px top/bottom padding — the quiet, still moment needs breathing room to contrast with the grid density above
- Section 5: 96px top/bottom padding — the CTA close needs space to feel like a conclusion, not a footer

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR
- Desktop (≥1280px): session grid is 3 columns; stats are 4 across; story block is 2-column split (text left, chart right)

BRUTALK INSTRUCTORS PAGE — FULL PAGE DESIGN DIRECTION

SECTION SEQUENCE AND RHYTHM:
The page opens with a confrontational, asymmetric page header that functions like a dojo entrance — heavy type, stark contrast, a raw silhouette grid illustration bleeding into the background. Section 2 explodes into a dense 4-column card grid roster where each card reads like a fighter's record — maximum information density, no softening. Section 3 deliberately breaks the grid rhythm with a full-bleed Alarm Red (#E8000D) story block — a single saturated panel of body copy that acts as a structural gut-punch, pausing the card catalog momentum to deliver institutional credibility. Section 4 returns to structure with a horizontal timeline rendered as a raw numbered pipeline — four heavy stage markers in a left-to-right sequence that reads like a process diagram pinned to a wall. Section 5 closes with a sparse, aggressive CTA block on Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) — headline at maximum display scale, two raw-styled action buttons, no decorative relief.

Rhythm logic: Dense → Denser → Full-bleed color break → Structured pipeline → Sparse confrontational close. The alternation between maximum density (sections 2, 4) and deliberate structural pauses (sections 3, 5) prevents the page from becoming an undifferentiated wall of cards. No two consecutive sections share the same skeleton.

COLOR AND SURFACE USAGE:
- Section 1 (Header): Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) headline, Alarm Red (#E8000D) eyebrow label and a single thick horizontal rule beneath the headline, Caution Stripe (#FFD600) used on a stat callout ("200+" rendered at display scale in the header).

TYPOGRAPHIC HIERARCHY:
- H1 (Section 1 headline): Arial Black, 96px desktop / 56px mobile, fully uppercase, tracking -0.02em, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-flush, weight 900.
- Eyebrow labels: VT323, 13px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.12em — used in sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
- "200+" stat callout in section 1 header: Arial Black, 120px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600), positioned as a raw typographic object overlapping the silhouette illustration — this is the SIGNATURE MOMENT (see below).
- H2 (Section 2 headline "THE ROSTER"): Arial Black, 64px, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-flush.

- Card body/description: Courier New, 14px, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), line-height 1.6.
- Card metadata badges (language, credential, years): VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600) on Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) background, tight padding, raw border.
- Section 3 headline: Arial Black, 72px, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) on Alarm Red background, left-flush.

- Section 5 headline: Arial Black, 80px desktop / 48px mobile, uppercase, Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2), left-flush, tracking -0.02em.

SIGNATURE MOMENT:
The page's signature visual moment lives at the top of Section 1 (Page Header). The number "200+" is set in Arial Black at 120px in Caution Stripe (#FFD600) and positioned as a raw, off-grid typographic object that overlaps and partially obscures the abstract silhouette illustration grid in the upper-right quadrant of the header. It does not sit beside the illustration — it crashes into it, bleeding partially off the right edge of the grid. This is a brutalist type-as-image gesture: the number is simultaneously data and design object, confrontational in scale, and unmistakably BRUTALK in register. No other page uses this specific move. It is calibrated to the brutalist aesthetic's visual cues of asymmetry, visible structure, and harsh contrast.

SIGNATURE MOTION MOMENT:
The "200+" Caution Stripe numeral in Section 1 slams into its final position from off-screen right — it slides in hard and fast (roughly 300ms), overshooting by a few pixels before snapping back to rest with a single sharp rebound. This happens approximately one beat after the main headline settles, drawing the eye to the number's scale and color. It should feel like a physical impact, not a smooth ease — matching the anti-polish brutalist register. No other section attempts this kind of kinetic aggression.

MOTION DESIGN — FULL PAGE ARC:
ON-LOAD: The page background (Brutalk Black) appears instantly. The eyebrow label in Section 1 fades in first, very quickly. The H1 headline slams in from the left — a fast, heavy translate-X entrance with no easing softness, landing hard. A beat after the headline settles, the "200+" Caution Stripe numeral crashes in from the right (the signature motion moment described above). The subheadline and body text in Section 1 fade up softly a beat after the numeral lands. The silhouette illustration grid fades in last, slightly slower, as if materializing behind the type.

SCROLL-TRIGGERED REVEALS: Section 2 card grid — cards stagger in from bottom (translate-Y, fade) in groups of 4 per row, each row triggering as it enters the viewport. The stagger within a row is tight — cards 1, 2, 3, 4 enter with a very short offset between them, making the row feel like it snaps into place. Section 3 (Alarm Red panel) — the entire block slides up from below as a single solid unit; no internal stagger, the block arrives as one mass. Section 4 timeline — stage markers and connector lines draw in sequentially left to right as the section enters the viewport: the connector line between stages extends as an animated stroke, then the next stage circle pops in. Section 5 CTA — headline slams in from left (same motion language as Section 1 H1), then the two CTA elements fade up a beat later.

HOVER AFFORDANCES: Instructor cards in Section 2 — on hover, a 4px Alarm Red (#E8000D) border appears on all four sides of the card (instant, no transition delay), and the card lifts 4px with no shadow (brutalist — no soft shadow, just displacement). Instructor name text shifts from Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) to Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2) on card hover. Primary CTA button in Section 5 — background shifts from Alarm Red to Caution Stripe (#FFD600), text shifts to Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A) on hover, quick 150ms transition. Secondary CTA link — underline thickens from 1px to 3px on hover, color stays Hyperlink Blue. Stage marker circles in Section 4 — fill with Alarm Red (#E8000D) on hover, numeral shifts to Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2).

AMBIENT LOOPED MOTION: A blinking cursor character ("|") rendered in VT323 at 14px in Alarm Red (#E8000D) is placed at the end of the eyebrow label in Section 1, blinking at a steady rhythm (on for ~600ms, off for ~400ms, looped). This is the only ambient looped motion on the page — brutalist restraint, one ambient gesture, placed at the most prominent entry point.

DENSITY AND WHITESPACE LOGIC:
Sections 1 and 2 are high-density — the header is packed with typographic objects at different scales, the grid is tight with 24px gutters between cards. Section 3 is deliberately spacious within its red panel — generous top/bottom padding (80px+) lets the body text breathe against the aggressive color. Section 4 has medium density — four stage blocks with clear separation. Section 5 is the sparsest section — maximum whitespace around the headline and two CTAs, letting the scale of the type do all the work.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR:
- Desktop (1280px+): Section 1 uses a 12-column grid — type occupies columns 1–7, illustration grid occupies columns 8–12 with the "200+" numeral overlapping from column 6 onward. Section 2 card grid: 4 columns. Section 3: full-bleed, single column of text centered in a max-width container. Section 4 timeline: horizontal, 4 stages side by side. Section 5: left-flush headline, CTAs inline below.
- Tablet (768–1279px): Section 1 stacks — illustration moves below type, "200+" numeral repositions to overlap the top of the illustration. Section 2: 2-column card grid. Section 4 timeline: 2x2 grid arrangement. Section 5: headline at 56px, CTAs stack vertically.
- Mobile (below 768px): Section 1: single column, H1 at 48px, "200+" at 80px. Section 2: single column, cards full width. Section 3: full-bleed red, body at 15px. Section 4: vertical stacked timeline, connector lines become vertical. Section 5: headline at 40px, CTAs full width stacked.

PAGE FIT WITHIN SHARED DESIGN SYSTEM:
This page uses every token from the shared palette and both primary typefaces (Arial Black for display, Courier New for body, VT323 for metadata/eyebrows). It is the most human-facing page on the site — the instructors are the credibility engine — but it resists the temptation to soften into warmth. The fighter's-record card structure, the Alarm Red full-bleed story block, and the raw vetting pipeline timeline all maintain the BRUTALK voice: blunt, bold, unpolished, direct. The page sits between the Classes overview (card-heavy, catalog energy) and the Pricing conversion page (sparse, decisive), and it earns its place by delivering human proof at full brutalist amplitude.

## BRUTALK — Pricing Page: Full Visual Design Direction

### Page Role & Tone
This is the conversion page — the visitor has already been sold by the rest of the site. The design job here is to remove friction, demolish hesitation, and make the act of choosing a plan feel inevitable. The page must feel like a posted notice — authoritative, blunt, zero-apology. No softening. No reassuring pastels. The brutalist register is at full amplitude: harsh contrast, monospace body copy, system-weight headings, visible structural grid lines, and a palette that uses black as the dominant ground with Alarm Red and Caution Stripe doing aggressive, purposeful work.

### Section Sequence & Rhythm
The five sections follow a deliberate density arc:
1. **Page Header** — sparse, confrontational, type-dominant. One moment of typographic aggression before anything else loads.
2. **Pricing Cards** — maximum structural density. Three-column card grid with a horizontal comparison chart below. The heaviest content block on the page.
3. **Stats** — a stark horizontal strip of four oversized numerals. Sparse, fast, punchy — a decompression beat after the card density.
4. **FAQ** — dense list block, side-tabbed or stacked index format. Returns to density but in a different shape (list vs. grid).
5. **CTA Close** — deliberately sparse again. One headline, two buttons, maximum negative space. The page exhales here.

The rhythm is: sparse → dense → sparse → dense → sparse. This alternation prevents the page from feeling like an unbroken wall of content while never drifting into the airy, polished register of a modern SaaS template.

### Color & Surface Usage
- **Brutalk Black (#0A0A0A):** Page background across all sections. No alternating off-white sections. The entire page sits on black — this is a deliberate commitment to the brutalist palette.
- **Concrete Slab (#1E1E1E):** Card surfaces for all three pricing cards and FAQ items. One step lighter than the page background — creates visible separation without softening.
- **Chalk Strike (#F2F2F2):** All primary text on dark surfaces — headlines, body, card titles, stat numbers.
- **Alarm Red (#E8000D):** The Committed plan card's top border (full-width 4px stroke), the primary CTA buttons, the "MOST POPULAR" badge on the Committed card, and — critically — the signature moment (see below). Also used for the stat strip's left-edge vertical rule.
- **Caution Stripe (#FFD600):** "LAST SEATS" or featured badges on cards if applicable, stat unit labels, and the eyebrow labels in VT323 across all sections.
- **Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE):** All FAQ toggle links, inline secondary links in card descriptions, and the "See the Schedule" secondary CTA.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- **H1 (Page Header headline):** Arial Black, 96px desktop / 52px mobile, fully uppercase, tracking -0.02em, left-flush, Chalk Strike on black. This is the typographic arrival.
- **H2 (Section headlines):** Arial Black, 56–64px desktop / 36px mobile, uppercase, left-flush.
- **Card titles (plan names + price):** Arial Black, 40px desktop, uppercase, Chalk Strike. Price rendered at 56px in Alarm Red on the Committed card, Chalk Strike on the others.
- **Body / descriptions:** Courier New, 15px, line-height 1.6, Chalk Strike. Reads like a typed document.
- **Eyebrow labels:** VT323, 13px, Caution Stripe (#FFD600), uppercase, letter-spacing 0.12em. Used above every section headline.
- **Stat numerals:** Arial Black, 80px desktop / 48px mobile, Chalk Strike. Stat labels in VT323 13px Caution Stripe below each numeral.
- **FAQ question labels:** Arial Black, 20px, uppercase, Chalk Strike.
- **FAQ answer text:** Courier New, 15px, Hyperlink Blue (#0000EE) — the deliberate browser-default link color applied to answer text signals raw, unstyled intentionality.

### Signature Moment: The Committed Plan Price Stamp
The signature visual moment lives in the Pricing Cards section. The Committed plan card — the middle of three — receives a full-height left border in Alarm Red (8px solid), a top-edge "MOST POPULAR" badge in Caution Stripe with VT323 text, and most critically: its price ($139) is rendered in Arial Black at 80px in Alarm Red, overflowing the card's top edge by approximately 20px so the numeral bleeds past the card boundary into the page background. This is a deliberately off-grid, anti-contained typographic move — the number refuses to stay inside its box. It is a structural brutalist gesture: the price is so important it cannot be contained. The other two cards' prices remain at 56px in Chalk Strike, fully contained. The contrast in scale and color makes the Committed plan feel selected without using any subtle highlighting tricks.

### Signature Motion Moment: Price Numeral Slam
On scroll-trigger as the pricing cards section enters the viewport, the three card columns slide up from below with a slight stagger (Starter first, Committed a beat later, Intensive a beat after that). As the Committed card settles, its overflowing $139 price numeral performs a single sharp downward "slam" — it drops 12px and snaps back to position in a quick, weighty motion (like a rubber stamp hitting paper). This happens once, on reveal, and is never repeated. It is loud, structural, and unmistakably brutalist — a motion that feels like emphasis rather than decoration.

### Motion Design: Full Arc
**On-load arc:**
- The page header headline ("WHAT IT COSTS. WHAT YOU GET. NOTHING HIDDEN.") arrives letter-by-letter in a fast left-to-right type-on effect — not a smooth fade, but a hard-cut character reveal, like a typewriter at high speed. This completes in under one second.
- The eyebrow label above the headline fades in a beat before the headline starts.
- The subheadline below slides up from 16px below its final position and fades in a beat after the headline completes.
- Everything else on the page is still on load — only the header section animates on arrival.

**Scroll-triggered reveals:**
- Pricing cards section: three cards slide up with stagger on IntersectionObserver trigger. The comparison chart below fades in after all three cards have settled.
- Stats section: the four stat numerals count up from zero to their final value when the section enters the viewport (the numbers tick upward rapidly and land on the real number). Stat descriptions fade in below each number after the count completes.
- FAQ section: each FAQ item slides in from the left, staggered one after another, as the section scrolls into view.
- CTA close section: the headline slams in at full opacity with no fade — hard cut, no transition — a beat before the two CTA buttons fade in below it.

**Hover & focus affordances:**
- Pricing cards: on hover, the card border shifts from 1px Concrete Slab to 2px Alarm Red. The card lifts 4px with a subtle shadow (no soft box-shadow — a hard offset shadow in Alarm Red, 4px right and 4px down). This is fast — under 150ms.
- CTA buttons: on hover, background flips from Alarm Red to Chalk Strike with text in Brutalk Black. Hard swap, no gradient transition.
- FAQ items: on hover, the question text shifts from Chalk Strike to Caution Stripe. The answer text (Hyperlink Blue) gains a text-underline.
- Secondary CTA links: standard Hyperlink Blue underline appears on hover — deliberately browser-default.

**Ambient looped motion:**
- The "MOST POPULAR" badge on the Committed card pulses with a slow, two-second opacity breathe (full opacity → 80% → full opacity, looped) — the only ambient motion on the page. It is deliberately restrained: one element, one loop, no distractions.
- A blinking cursor character (█) appears at the end of the page header headline after the type-on completes — it blinks at a steady one-second interval, like a terminal cursor. This is ambient and persistent until the user scrolls past the header.

**Calibration note:** Motion intensity is deliberately low for this brutalist page. The type-on headline, the pricing card stagger + price slam, the stat count-up, and the badge pulse are the full motion vocabulary. Everything else is still or responds only to hover. Brutalist motion should feel like structural emphasis, not performance.

### Layout & Grid
- Desktop: 12-column grid, 24px gutters, max-width 1280px, centered with left-flush content alignment inside.
- Pricing cards: three equal columns (4 columns each), with the Committed card's price numeral overflowing its top edge.
- Stats strip: four equal columns (3 columns each), no card surfaces — numerals float on the black page background.
- FAQ: single column, full-width list, 640px max-width content column left-aligned (not centered).
- CTA close: full-bleed black panel, text left-aligned at 56px H2 scale, buttons left-aligned in a row.

### Responsive Behavior
- Mobile (< 768px): Pricing cards stack to single column. Committed card appears first (reordered to top). Price numeral overflow is reduced to 10px. Stats strip wraps to 2×2 grid. FAQ remains single column. CTA close headline drops to 36px. All type scales reduce proportionally. The brutalist character is preserved — no softening of borders, no removal of Alarm Red accents.
- Tablet (768–1024px): Pricing cards remain three-column but at reduced padding. Stats strip stays 4-column. FAQ and CTA close unchanged.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses every color in the shared palette with purpose — Brutalk Black as ground, Chalk Strike as primary text, Alarm Red as the aggressive conversion accent, Caution Stripe for eyebrows and badges, Hyperlink Blue for FAQ answers and secondary links, Concrete Slab for card surfaces. Typography follows the system exactly: Arial Black for all headings, Courier New for all body, VT323 for all eyebrow/metadata labels. The page is unmistakably BRUTALK — it does not borrow from any other aesthetic register.
